critical_takeaway.stopping_penetration_vs_surviving_blunt_: Unarmored human thorax suffers lethal penetration and catastrophic local BFD (>80 mm, VC > 5 m/s). Flexible keratin scales arrest fragments and 9mm, but high momentum threats (.44 Mag, 7.62mm rifle) cause lethal Behind-Armor Blunt Trauma (BFD > 45 mm, VC > 1.2 m/s). Only rigid, skeletal-bridged osteoderm composites (focal dispersion >= 120 mm) reduce 9mm BFD to <20 mm (AIS 1-2). For high-velocity rifle projectiles (7.62x39mm), biological armor without an external rigid frame leaves a residual ~35% lethality risk from sheer momentum transfer.
